title: Cole Slaws
directions: Toss all vegetables in a large bowl with 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper.
Whisk together mayonnaise, vinegar, and sugar, then toss with slaw.
Chill, covered, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes (for vegetables to wilt and flavors to blend).
Serve at room temperature or chilled.
If you want any extra kick you can use Greek yogurt instead of sour cream, or add some extra vinegar, or celery seeds or salt, or mustard, or even shredded apples.
Combine cabbage, bell pepper, cilantro, and jalapeño in large bowl; toss to blend.
Whisk oil, lime juice, and cumin in small bowl to blend.
Pour dressing over cabbage mixture. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Chill, covered, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes (for vegetables to wilt and flavors to blend).
Serve at room temperature or chilled.
Whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar, sugar, and ½ teaspoon each of salt and pepper in a large bowl until combined well.
Then toss with cabbage and carrots.
Chill, covered, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes (for vegetables to wilt and flavors to blend).
Serve at room temperature or chilled.
Most coleslaws develop extra flavor with an overnight marinating and occasional stirring.
If the slaw gets too juicy, just pour off some of the liquid before serving.
This finely chopped slaw has a nice balance of sweet and tart. It can go on top of a sandwich, such as pulled pork, not just alongside it.
If you like them, you can use green peppers rather than red ones.
